# Sirach Chapter 37 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 37 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_037_page_001.jpg

---

**37:1** Every companion says, "I too am your friend," but there is a companion who is a friend in name only.

**37:2** Is it not a grief to the point of death when a close companion turns into an enemy?

**37:3** O evil impulse! Why were you formed only to cover the land with treachery?

**37:4** A false companion gloats over a friend's good fortune, but in time of trouble turns against him.

**37:5** A loyal companion fights alongside a friend against the enemy and stands firm against an adversary.

**37:6** Do not forget a friend in battle, and do not neglect him when dividing the spoils.

**37:7** Every adviser gives advice, but some advise only in their own interest.

**37:8** Be on your guard against a counselor, and first learn what his stake is — for he counsels for his own advantage — lest he cast the lot against you.

**37:9** He may say to you, "Your path is a good one," while standing nearby to see how you fare.

**37:10** Do not take counsel from someone who eyes you with suspicion, nor disclose your plans to those who envy you.

**37:11** Do not consult a woman about her rival, or a coward about war, a merchant about business matters, or a buyer about selling, an envious person about gratitude, an unmerciful person about kindness, a lazy person about any kind of work, a temporary worker about completing the job, or an idle servant about serious undertakings. Disregard all such when seeking advice.

**37:12** Instead, associate regularly with a godly person whom you have observed to keep the commandments, whose life is in harmony with your own, and who will grieve with you if you fall.

**37:13** But also trust in the counsel of your own heart, for no one is more reliable to you than it is.

**37:14** For a person's own mind can notify him better than seven sentinels posted on a height.

**37:15** But above all this, pray to the Most High to guide your steps in truth.

**37:16** The starting point of every deed is a word, and before every action comes forethought.

**37:17** The source of all human activity is the heart; it sends out four branches —

**37:18** good and evil, life and death — and the tongue, which governs all of them, has unceasing mastery.

**37:19** There is someone who is clever and the teacher of many, yet is useless to himself.

**37:20** An eloquent speaker may be hated; he will be deprived of everything,

**37:21** for grace was not given him by the Lord, since he is devoid of all wisdom.

**37:22** There is a person who is wise for his own benefit, and the fruits of his discernment are reliable.

**37:23** A wise person instructs his own people, and the fruits of his understanding are dependable.

**37:24** A wise person will be filled with blessings, and all who see him will declare him fortunate.

**37:25** The life of a person spans few days, but the life of Israel has no limit.

**37:26** One who is wise among his people will receive a heritage of honor, and his name will live on forever.

**37:27** My child, test yourself throughout your lifetime; note what is harmful to you and do not give yourself to it.

**37:28** For not everything benefits everyone, and not every soul is pleased by the same thing.

**37:29** Do not be greedy for every delicacy, and do not be excessive in your eating.

**37:30** For overeating leads to illness, and gluttony brings on stomach pain.

**37:31** Many have died from gluttony, but whoever is disciplined will add to life.
